lessons.title: Découvrons l'art des fêtes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize that art is used to celebrate special times

opening.activity: Show holiday art images from different cultures. Use gestures to show 'celebration' (clapping, dancing). Say 'C'est l'art!' while pointing to decorative items. Connect to students' experiences: 'Avez-vous vu l'art pour les fêtes?'
opening.visualSupports: Photo cards of holiday decorations, festive art from various traditions

main.activity: Gallery walk around classroom with holiday art examples. Students draw one thing they see that celebrates. Practice saying 'fête', 'art', 'célébrer' with actions. Create a class list of where we see celebration art.
main.visualSupports: Picture cards, gesture cards for vocabulary, drawing templates if needed

closing.activity: Share one drawing with a partner. Practice saying 'C'est l'art pour célébrer.' Clean up materials together.
closing.visualSupports: Sentence strip with French phrase, cleanup picture schedule

troubleshooting.then: If materials missing: Use classroom decorations as examples. If too complex: Just look at and name holiday colors in room.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students see art in decorations at home and in community

lessons.title: Les couleurs de l'hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify winter colors in holiday art

opening.activity: Review Lesson 1: 'Hier, nous avons vu l'art des fêtes.' Show winter scene photos. Point to colors and say 'couleur'. Demonstrate winter colors with paint swatches.
opening.visualSupports: Color cards, winter photographs, paint swatches

main.activity: Color hunt around room for winter colors. Sort color cards into 'hiver' and 'pas hiver' groups. Paint or color with winter palette. Create simple winter color collage.
main.visualSupports: Color sorting mats, winter vs summer color comparison charts

closing.activity: Show collages to class. Practice 'Voici les couleurs d'hiver.' Vote on favorite winter color as class.
closing.visualSupports: Sentence strips, color voting board

troubleshooting.then: If art supplies unavailable: Use crayons to circle winter colors in magazines. If time short: Just sort pre-made color cards.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Winter colors appear in nature and holiday decorations around them

lessons.title: Mes traditions familiales
lessons.oneGoal: Students will share their family traditions through simple drawings

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 2: 'Nous avons vu les couleurs d'hiver.' Show family celebration photos (diverse traditions). Use gesture for 'famille' (group hug motion). Say 'Chaque famille a des traditions.'
opening.visualSupports: Diverse family celebration photos, gesture cards

main.activity: Students draw their family's way of celebrating (any tradition). Walk around, ask 'Qu'est-ce que c'est?' Practice vocabulary while drawing. Share with table partners.
main.visualSupports: Tradition example cards, vocabulary picture cards, drawing step guides

closing.activity: Gallery walk of family tradition drawings. Practice 'Ma famille...' sentence starter. Appreciate diversity with 'C'est beau!'
closing.visualSupports: Sentence starter cards, appreciation phrase cards

troubleshooting.then: If drawing too complex: Just talk about traditions with picture cards. If sensitive family situations: Focus on classroom traditions instead.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Every family has special ways to celebrate that can be shown through art

lessons.title: Créons ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students will work together to create a class winter art piece

opening.activity: Review Lesson 3: 'Hier, vous avez dessiné vos traditions.' Demonstrate 'ensemble' by bringing hands together. Show large blank paper: 'Nous allons créer ensemble!'
opening.visualSupports: Hand gesture cards, large collaborative space setup

main.activity: Class collaborates on large winter scene. Each student adds one element. Practice turn-taking and French phrases: 'À mon tour', 'Très beau', 'Ensemble c'est mieux.'
main.visualSupports: Turn-taking cards, collaborative work examples, phrase strips

closing.activity: Step back and admire class creation. Practice 'Nous avons créé ensemble!' Take a class photo with the art.
closing.visualSupports: Achievement celebration cards, photo props

troubleshooting.then: If collaboration too difficult: Work in pairs instead of whole class. If materials insufficient: Use drawing on shared paper.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Communities work together to create beautiful holiday displays

lessons.title: Formes de l'hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create winter shapes using basic geometric forms

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 4: 'Hier, nous avons créé ensemble.' Show winter objects (snowflake, tree, ornament). Trace shapes in air: 'Voici un rond, un triangle.' Use body to make shapes.
opening.visualSupports: Large shape cards, winter object photos, shape tracing guides

main.activity: Shape hunt in winter pictures. Students trace and cut basic shapes. Combine shapes to make winter objects (triangle trees, round snowmen). Practice shape names while creating.
main.visualSupports: Shape sorting mats, winter object assembly guides, vocabulary cards

closing.activity: Shape show-and-tell: 'J'ai fait un... avec des...' Display creations on shape sorting board.
closing.visualSupports: Sentence starter cards, shape display board

troubleshooting.then: If scissors unavailable: Tear shapes from paper or use pre-cut shapes. If too complex: Just identify shapes in pictures.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Winter symbols like snowflakes, trees, and ornaments all use basic shapes

lessons.title: Décorations simples
lessons.oneGoal: Students will make simple decorations using paper and basic materials

opening.activity: Review Lesson 5: 'Hier, nous avons fait des formes.' Show simple paper decorations. Demonstrate 'décoration' by hanging one up. Practice scissor safety: 'Attention avec les ciseaux!'
opening.visualSupports: Decoration examples, safety poster for scissors, step-by-step photos

main.activity: Students make paper chain decorations or simple snowflakes. Focus on safe scissor use and following steps. Practice vocabulary while creating: 'Je coupe le papier.'
main.visualSupports: Step-by-step instruction cards, safety reminders, finished examples

closing.activity: Hang decorations around classroom. Practice 'Voici ma décoration!' Admire everyone's work with 'C'est joli!'
closing.visualSupports: Appreciation phrase cards, decoration display area

troubleshooting.then: If scissors concerns arise: Use tear-decorations or pre-cut pieces. If time short: Make simple paper chains only.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Families make decorations together to beautify their homes

lessons.title: Cartes de souhaits
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create greeting cards with winter symbols

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 6: 'Hier, nous avons fait des décorations.' Show greeting cards from different cultures. Open and close cards: 'C'est une carte!' Point to winter symbols: 'Voici des symboles.'
opening.visualSupports: Various greeting cards, winter symbol chart, gesture cards

main.activity: Students create greeting cards with winter symbols. Add simple French messages like 'Bonne fête!' or draw pictures to communicate. Practice vocabulary while decorating.
main.visualSupports: French greeting examples, symbol reference sheet, card folding guide

closing.activity: Share cards with partners. Practice 'Voici ma carte!' Discuss who they might give cards to: 'Pour ma famille!'
closing.visualSupports: Sharing sentence strips, family vocabulary cards

troubleshooting.then: If card-making too complex: Decorate pre-made cards. If writing difficult: Focus only on pictures and symbols.

lessons.realWorldConnection: People send cards to share love and good wishes during celebrations

lessons.title: Cadeaux faits main
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create simple handmade gifts

opening.activity: Review Lesson 7: 'Hier, nous avons fait des cartes.' Show handmade gifts. Use hands to demonstrate 'fait à la main.' Practice 'C'est un cadeau!' with giving gestures.
opening.visualSupports: Handmade gift examples, hand gesture cards, giving motion pictures

main.activity: Students create simple gifts (decorated containers, bookmarks, painted stones). Focus on the care in making something for someone else. Practice 'Je donne un cadeau.'
main.visualSupports: Gift-making step guides, caring gesture cards, finished examples

closing.activity: Wrap gifts in simple materials. Practice 'C'est fait avec amour!' Discuss the joy of giving vs. receiving.
closing.visualSupports: Emotion cards, giving vs. receiving pictures

troubleshooting.then: If craft supplies limited: Decorate paper bags as gifts. If too complex: Make simple drawings as gifts.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Handmade gifts show extra care and thoughtfulness

lessons.title: Textures d'hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore different textures in winter-themed art

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 8: 'Hier, nous avons fait des cadeaux.' Touch different materials: cotton (soft snow), sandpaper (rough bark). Practice 'doux' and 'rugueux' with facial expressions.
opening.visualSupports: Texture sample board, expression cards for soft/rough, winter texture photos

main.activity: Texture exploration station. Students feel materials and sort into 'doux' and 'rugueux.' Create winter collages using different textures to represent snow, trees, ice.
main.visualSupports: Texture sorting mats, winter scene examples, texture vocabulary cards

closing.activity: Touch and describe textures: 'C'est doux comme...' 'C'est rugueux comme...' Display texture art gallery-style.
closing.visualSupports: Comparison sentence starters, texture description cards

troubleshooting.then: If texture materials unavailable: Use classroom objects for texture exploration. If sensory issues: Make texture exploration optional.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Winter brings different textures - soft snow, rough bark, smooth ice

lessons.title: Lumières et ombres
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create art showing light and shadow effects

opening.activity: Review Lesson 9: 'Hier, nous avons touché les textures.' Darken room, use flashlight to create shadows. Point to light: 'C'est la lumière!' Point to shadow: 'C'est l'ombre!'
opening.visualSupports: Light/shadow demonstration setup, vocabulary cards with symbols

main.activity: Shadow play with objects and flashlights. Students trace shadows on paper. Create 'light' pictures with bright colors and 'shadow' pictures with dark colors.
main.visualSupports: Shadow tracing guides, light/dark color examples, holiday light photos

closing.activity: Compare light and shadow artworks. Practice 'Voici la lumière, voici l'ombre.' Connect to holiday lights they've seen.
closing.visualSupports: Light/shadow comparison charts, holiday light examples

troubleshooting.then: If flashlights unavailable: Use window light for shadows. If too dark in room: Focus on bright/dark color concepts only.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Holiday celebrations often feature special lighting and candles

lessons.title: Motifs répétés
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create patterns using winter and holiday motifs

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 10: 'Hier, nous avons vu la lumière et l'ombre.' Show patterned holiday decorations. Demonstrate 'répéter' by repeating actions. Point to patterns: 'Voici un motif!'
opening.visualSupports: Patterned decoration examples, repetition demonstration cards, motif identification sheets

main.activity: Pattern detective hunt in room. Students identify repeating motifs. Create their own patterns using winter stamps or drawings. Practice 'Je répète le motif.'
main.visualSupports: Pattern identification guides, winter motif reference sheets, pattern creation templates

closing.activity: Pattern show and tell. Students describe their patterns: 'Mon motif répète...' Create class pattern book.
closing.visualSupports: Pattern description sentence starters, class book template

troubleshooting.then: If stamps unavailable: Use finger painting for patterns. If too complex: Just identify existing patterns in room.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Traditional holiday decorations often feature repeating patterns

lessons.title: Mon chef-d'œuvre
lessons.oneGoal: Students will combine all learned techniques in a personal masterpiece

opening.activity: Review all previous lessons with visual reminders. Explain 'chef-d'œuvre' as 'your best art.' Show how artists 'combiner' different techniques. Let students choose their focus.
opening.visualSupports: Lesson review poster, technique choice board, masterpiece examples

main.activity: Students create their masterpiece using any combination of learned techniques (shapes, colors, textures, patterns, etc.). Circulate and practice vocabulary: 'J'ai combiné...'
main.visualSupports: Technique reminder cards, planning templates, step-by-step guides

closing.activity: Students place masterpieces in portfolios. Practice 'C'est mon chef-d'œuvre!' Plan for sharing in next lesson.
closing.visualSupports: Portfolio labels, sharing preparation cards

troubleshooting.then: If choices overwhelming: Assign specific technique combinations. If time short: Focus on one favorite technique only.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Artists combine different skills to create meaningful works

lessons.title: Galerie de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will display and discuss their artwork like in a real gallery

opening.activity: Connect to Lesson 12: 'Hier, vous avez fini vos chef-d'œuvres!' Set up classroom like art gallery. Practice gallery manners: quiet walking, careful looking. Demonstrate 'montrer' and 'expliquer.'
opening.visualSupports: Gallery setup photos, gallery behavior cards, presentation gesture guides

main.activity: Gallery walk where students present their masterpieces. Practice 'Voici mon art. J'ai utilisé...' Other students practice appreciation: 'C'est beau!' 'J'aime...'
main.visualSupports: Presentation sentence starters, appreciation phrase cards, gallery viewing guides

closing.activity: Vote for favorite gallery experience (not artwork). Practice 'Notre galerie est magnifique!' Take photos for portfolios.
closing.visualSupports: Gallery reflection cards, photo permission and props

troubleshooting.then: If gallery setup impossible: Do table-to-table sharing. If presentations too long: Limit to one technique per student.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Artists display their work for others to enjoy and appreciate

lessons.title: Réflexion artistique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will reflect on their learning and artistic growth

opening.activity: Review journey from Lesson 1 to 13 using visual timeline. Practice 'réflexion' by thinking gesture. Show growth from first drawings to masterpieces: 'Vous avez grandi!'
opening.visualSupports: Learning journey timeline, growth comparison examples, thinking gesture cards

main.activity: Students look through portfolios and identify learning. Complete simple reflection sheets with drawings/words. Practice 'J'ai appris...' 'Je peux maintenant...' Share growth with partners.
main.visualSupports: Reflection sheet templates, learning vocabulary cards, portfolio organization guides

closing.activity: Class celebration of artistic growth. Practice 'Nous sommes des artistes!' Plan how to share learning with families.
closing.visualSupports: Celebration materials, artist identity cards, family sharing planning sheets

troubleshooting.then: If reflection too abstract: Focus on favorite artworks only. If time limited: Do verbal reflection circle only.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Artists always reflect on their work to continue growing

lessons.title: Art collaboratif
lessons.oneGoal: Students will work together on a large collaborative winter mural

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Review collaborative work from Lesson 4. Show large mural space. Plan together what winter scene to create. Assign roles based on student strengths and interests.
opening.visualSupports: Mural planning sheets, role cards, collaborative work examples

main.activity: Students work in assigned roles to create mural sections. Practice collaborative vocabulary and problem-solving. Combine individual sections into cohesive whole.
main.visualSupports: Section planning guides, collaborative vocabulary reminders, problem-solving strategy cards

closing.activity: Step back and admire collaborative mural. Celebrate teamwork and individual contributions. Display prominently in school.
closing.visualSupports: Teamwork celebration cards, display planning materials

troubleshooting.then: If mural too ambitious: Create smaller collaborative pieces. If collaboration breaking down: Return to individual work within group project.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Community art projects bring people together

lessons.title: Techniques avancées
lessons.oneGoal: Students will experiment with more advanced art techniques

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Show advanced techniques (watercolor blending, printmaking, mixed media). Let students choose which techniques to explore. Set up exploration stations.
opening.visualSupports: Technique demonstration cards, station setup guides, choice boards

main.activity: Station rotation where students try advanced techniques. Focus on experimentation and discovery rather than perfection. Document techniques they enjoy most.
main.visualSupports: Station instruction cards, technique documentation sheets, discovery celebration materials

closing.activity: Share favorite new techniques discovered. Plan which ones to use in future projects. Celebrate willingness to try new things.
closing.visualSupports: Technique sharing cards, future planning sheets, risk-taking celebration materials

troubleshooting.then: If advanced supplies unavailable: Modify familiar techniques in new ways. If techniques too challenging: Focus on perfecting basic techniques.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Artists continually learn new ways to express themselves

lessons.title: Art numérique simple
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore basic digital art tools for winter themes

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Show digital art examples alongside traditional art. Demonstrate simple digital tools. Connect to winter themes they've explored in previous lessons.
opening.visualSupports: Digital vs traditional art comparison, simple tool demonstration, winter theme examples

main.activity: Students explore simple digital drawing tools to create winter scenes. Focus on how digital tools can create effects similar to traditional techniques. Save and share digital creations.
main.visualSupports: Digital tool guides, winter scene templates, sharing instruction cards

closing.activity: Compare digital and traditional winter artworks. Discuss benefits of each medium. Display digital art alongside traditional pieces.
closing.visualSupports: Medium comparison charts, display planning materials, reflection cards

troubleshooting.then: If technology issues: Use traditional tools to create 'digital-style' effects. If apps too complex: Use simpler drawing programs.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Modern artists use both traditional and digital tools

lessons.title: Art recyclé
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create winter art using recycled materials

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Show recycled art examples. Discuss how artists can help environment by reusing materials. Sort available recycled materials by type and potential use.
opening.visualSupports: Recycled art examples, environmental care books, material sorting guides

main.activity: Students create winter sculptures or collages using recycled materials. Focus on creative problem-solving and seeing new possibilities in discarded items.
main.visualSupports: Creative reuse idea cards, winter theme guides, problem-solving strategy reminders

closing.activity: Recycled art showcase. Discuss how art can help care for our planet. Plan classroom recycling art collection.
closing.visualSupports: Environmental care celebration materials, recycling collection planning sheets

troubleshooting.then: If recycled materials unavailable: Use classroom paper scraps for collage. If safety concerns: Pre-sort materials more carefully.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Artists can create beauty while caring for our planet

lessons.title: Performance artistique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will combine visual art with movement and music

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Show how art can be combined with music and movement. Demonstrate creating art while music plays. Practice winter movements (falling snow, growing trees).
opening.visualSupports: Multi-art examples, movement demonstration cards, winter movement guides

main.activity: Students create art while winter music plays, incorporating movement into creation process. Paint to music rhythms, dance while creating, use art tools as musical instruments.
main.visualSupports: Movement-art integration guides, rhythm visual aids, creative expression examples

closing.activity: Performance showcase where students present art with movement or music. Celebrate creative expression and multi-art connections.
closing.visualSupports: Performance celebration materials, multi-art appreciation cards

troubleshooting.then: If performance too overwhelming: Focus on creating art while listening to music. If space limited: Do individual art-music connections at desks.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Many celebrations combine different art forms together

lessons.title: Célébration finale
lessons.oneGoal: Students will share their complete winter art journey with families

opening.activity: EXTENSION: Prepare for family celebration. Organize portfolios and select pieces to display. Practice sharing their learning journey with simple French phrases.
opening.visualSupports: Portfolio organization guides, presentation phrase cards, celebration planning materials

main.activity: Family celebration event. Students present portfolios, demonstrate techniques, and share favorite artworks. Families participate in simple art activity together.
main.visualSupports: Presentation guides, family activity instructions, celebration setup materials

closing.activity: Celebration reflection. Students share favorite moments from art journey. Plan continued art exploration. Thank families for support.
closing.visualSupports: Journey reflection materials, future planning cards, gratitude expression guides

troubleshooting.then: If family event not possible: Celebrate with other classes or school community. If time limited: Focus on student reflection and pride in achievements.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Art brings families and communities together in celebration
